title: NEXP versus nonuniform \(\mathrm{TC}^{0}\)
formal: Is there a language \(\mathrm{L}\in \mathrm{NEXP}\) such that, for every fixed circuit depth \(d\ge 1\), every fixed exponent \(k\ge 1\), every constant \(C\ge 1\) and every \(N\ge 1\), some \(n\ge N\) has no depth-at-most-d Boolean circuit of size at most \(C(n+1)^{k}\) with AND, OR, NOT and majority gates that computes L correctly on every n-bit input? Equivalently, is \(\mathrm{NEXP}\not\subset \mathrm{TC}^{0}\) for nonuniform \(\mathrm{TC}^{0}\)?
why: Tests whether the algorithmic approach to circuit lower bounds can cross the threshold-gate barrier.

progress.text: Williams separates nondeterministic exponential time from polynomial-size ACC circuits, a subclass of \(\mathrm{TC}^{0}\).
Chen–Tal–Wang prove \(n^{2.5- \varepsilon}\) gate lower bounds for depth-two threshold circuits and a hard function in \(E^{\mathrm{NP}}\).
Ren–Williams prove near-maximum unrestricted bounds for a class with a promise-MA oracle and advice.
Near-cubic depth-two wire bounds are claimed in a preprint with a critical source comment; this is not a \(\mathrm{TC}^{0}\) separation.

definitions: \(\mathrm{NEXP}=\bigcup _{a\ge 1}\mathrm{NTIME}(2^{n^{a}}): a\) language is accepted by one nondeterministic Turing machine whose every computation branch halts within exponential time \(2^{n^{a}}\), up to a constant factor, for some fixed a. An input is in the language exactly when at least one branch accepts. A circuit is a finite directed acyclic graph with n Boolean inputs, constants 0 and 1 and one output. AND and OR may have any positive fan-in; NOT has one input. A majority gate on m inputs outputs 1 when at least \(\lceil m/2\rceil\) of them are 1, including a tie when m is even. Fan-out is unrestricted. Size is the number of operation gates plus wires. Repeated connections count individually, so their multiplicities cannot encode uncharged weights. Depth is the maximum number of operation gates on an input-to-output path. All circuits compute exactly on every input; no average-case correctness or randomness is allowed. \(\mathrm{TC}^{0}\) consists of languages having one fixed depth bound and one polynomial size bound across all input lengths. The family may be nonuniform: no algorithm is required to construct its nth circuit. NEXP machines are uniform and have no oracle or advice. The formal quantifiers permit the lower bound to be witnessed at infinitely many input lengths, rather than requiring failure at every sufficiently large length.
answer_criterion: A positive resolution proves that one language in NEXP has no polynomial-size constant-depth majority-circuit family, with depth and polynomial exponent both unrestricted constants. A negative resolution proves \(\mathrm{NEXP}\subseteq \mathrm{TC}^{0}\). A bound ruling out only \(n^{k}\) gates for one fixed k, or only one fixed circuit depth, does not by itself establish the displayed separation.

context_blocks.title: Small depth still permits powerful gates
context_blocks.text: A constant-depth circuit applies only a bounded number of layers, but a majority gate can inspect many inputs at once. For three bits it returns 1 on 110 and 111, while returning 0 on 100. Thus majority is not a bounded-fan-in local operation. \(\mathrm{TC}^{0}\) permits many such gates in parallel and lets their outputs feed later layers. The depth bound stays fixed as input length grows, while the number of gates and wires may be any fixed polynomial.

context_blocks.title: Why parity is not enough
context_blocks.text: Parity is difficult for constant-depth circuits using only AND, OR and NOT, but it is easy for majority circuits. A threshold test for whether an n-bit input has at least t ones is implementable with a majority gate and suitable constants. Two adjacent threshold tests identify an exact number of ones, and taking an OR over odd counts gives parity with a polynomial number of gates in constant depth. This example shows why a lower bound for the weaker gate set cannot simply be reused after majority is added.

context_blocks.title: What NEXP contributes
context_blocks.text: The hard language need only have a nondeterministic exponential-time algorithm; it need not be in P or NP. That is a generous uniform computation budget, making the lack of a known separation striking. Nevertheless, counting the truth tables that have no small circuits does not automatically identify one language within this budget. The assertion requires one language that defeats every fixed polynomial size and every fixed depth, rather than a different unrestricted truth table for each desired bound.

context_blocks.title: The established nearby separation
context_blocks.text: Williams proves that NEXP does not have polynomial-size ACC circuits. ACC allows constant-depth Boolean circuits with gates testing the number of 1 inputs modulo a fixed integer. \(\mathrm{TC}^{0}\) can implement these modular tests by combining threshold comparisons. It is therefore a more permissive class, and excluding ACC does not exclude \(\mathrm{TC}^{0}\). The original 2011 reference supports this nearby theorem, not the stronger conclusion asked here.

context_blocks.title: The 2026 results retain important restrictions
context_blocks.text: Chen, Tal and Wang prove super-quadratic gate lower bounds for depth-two linear-threshold circuits, with a hard function in \(E^{\mathrm{NP}}\), exponential time with an NP oracle. Their \(n^{2.5- \varepsilon}\) bound is still a fixed polynomial and addresses depth two. A September preprint claims near-cubic wire bounds in that setting; its source also carries a critical comment, and it is not independently verified here. Wire counts and gate counts are different quantitative parameters. Ren and Williams obtain near-maximum general circuit bounds with a promise-Merlin–Arthur oracle and one bit of advice. None of these statements supplies the required ordinary NEXP language outside all of nonuniform \(\mathrm{TC}^{0}\).

sentences: Does some NEXP language escape all polynomial-size constant-depth majority circuits?
Majority gates make this circuit class substantially more powerful than constant-depth \(\mathrm{AND}/\mathrm{OR}\) circuits.
Williams established the corresponding separation for ACC circuits with fixed-modulus gates.
Recent threshold-circuit bounds still restrict depth or polynomial size and use different hard-language classes.
The target requires one ordinary NEXP language outside the entire nonuniform class \(\mathrm{TC}^{0}\).
